text: I'll start by looking at the workspace structure and the CSV import code.

The root cause is clear: line 18 forcibly encodes the whole input to ASCII with `errors="ignore"`, which silently drops every non-ASCII character. I'll check the tests before changing it so I don't break any expectations.
The test `test_preserves_unicode_customer_names` confirms the expected behavior. I'll remove the lossy ASCII round-trip so the text is parsed as Unicode.
All 29 tests pass, including the Unicode-preservation test.

args.summary: Root cause: `parse_orders_csv` in library/csv_import.py began by doing `text.encode("ascii", errors="ignore").decode("ascii")`, which silently strips every non-ASCII character from the whole CSV before parsing. That's why "José Martínez" became "Jos Martnez". I removed that lossy ASCII round-trip line so the input text is parsed with its Unicode characters intact. The full test suite passes (29/29), including test_preserves_unicode_customer_names. No test files were modified.
